highlights: home-assistant (29,195 files, 19,626 code files): graph time 810 → 566 s after the B2 fixes → 271 s after the speed commit (b479eadf0); 474k code edges, identical before and after.

Same repo, rerun 2026-10-21: Graphify 0.9.92 took 1,880 s (31 min) and 10.2 GB, 6.9× PipesHub's time; codebase-memory-mcp 110 s and 5 GB (0.11.0). PipesHub is the only one writing to a database server.

Speed commit b479eadf0: every repo builds 2–3× faster than at the PR's previous head, with every edge set byte-identical (all 9 B1 repos plus home-assistant). PipesHub is now faster than Graphify 0.9.92 on home-assistant (6.9×), pipeshub-ai backend (1.6×) and client-go (1.6×), even on django, and slower on guava and the small and TypeScript repos.
find_symbol_path on the large tier: p95 30.3 s → 63 ms (B2-G2). pipeshub-ai frontend median 130 → 13 ms (B2-G6).
Graph time fell 27–30% on the largest repos (django, pipeshub-ai backend, home-assistant). Block projection is still the largest stage: what remains is Neo4j's own write work (B2-G3, partly fixed).
Money is small: home-assistant costs about $0.70 to embed and about $2.88 of LLM classification input at small-model prices; the default local embedding model costs nothing.
method: Each repo goes through PipesHub's production write path into a fresh Neo4j 5.26 with the shipped settings (2 GB heap, 1 GB page cache, 3 GB and 4 CPU limit, APOC): code file records, parse and block projection, then the edge builder. Measured: time per stage, Neo4j memory and store size, graph size, embedding tokens (the indexer's own code units and tokenizer), LLM classification calls (the production skip policy), and p50/p95 latency of three agent tools on 50 symbols. The graph is read back from Neo4j and scored against the B1 truth.
question: How much time, memory and money does the graph cost as repos grow?
repos: The nine B1 projects (126 to 7,010 files) plus home-assistant/core as the large tier: 29,197 files, 19,634 Python, chosen because Python is where PipesHub's accuracy is highest. No truth for it: scale only.
summary: After the B2 fixes, a 20k-file Python monorepo indexes into Neo4j in 4.5 minutes (13.5 before the B2 fixes, 9.5 after them, 271 s after the speed commit), inside the shipped 3 GB Neo4j limit, and the graph read back from Neo4j scores exactly what B1 scored in memory. Agent tools answer in 4–14 ms at the median and under 0.25 s at p95 on every repo. The run found 8 gaps: 5 fixed, 1 partly fixed, 1 open, 1 kept by decision.
